explanation: In C++, the default access specifier determines the accessibility of members within a class or struct when no explicit access modifier is specified. For structs, members are public by default, meaning they can be accessed from outside the struct without restrictions. This feature simplifies the declaration of data structures intended for data storage without encapsulation, aligning with C++'s support for both procedural and object-oriented programming paradigms.
keywords: struct default access, C++ struct access specifier, struct members public
